thread:
elaine: FYI — Northbound just opened a support ticket, their calls to /v1/generate are returning 504s intermittently since 09:02 UTC. p95 jumped from 450ms to ~13s, p99 ~78s. Looks correlated with a request surge from the tenant.
chris: Thanks — any error traces or gateway logs yet?
elaine: Adding snippets from the gateway around the spike:
```
2026-03-15T09:02:14.123Z ERROR gateway req_id=ab12 status=504 tenant=northbound queue_depth=486 batcher_wait_ms=7518 route=/v1/generate model=gpt-medium-kv alloc_gpus=1
2026-03-15T09:02:20.678Z WARN  gateway req_id=ab47 status=503 tenant=northbound queue_depth=498 batcher_wait_ms=12045
```
chris: queue_depth ~500 is near our node-level cap (512). Is this the continuous-batcher backlog we saw last month?
olga: Looks like it — Batchers are backing up because of long-context requests with big KV cache growth. Northbound started sending concurrent longseq prompts ~>8k tokens. That increases per-request runtime and KV usage, so batch formation stalls.
mike: Can we confirm per-batcher queueing? Run the batcher debug endpoint on the pool handling hosted-prod-3.
elaine: I ran the quick check: `/ops/batcher/debug?pool=hosted-prod-3` output (summarized):
```
batcher_id=bp-03 inflight=34 queued=472 max_queue=512 avg_kv_size=1.9GB top_tenant=northbound tail_latency_p99=74s
```
jaya: Oof. avg_kv_size 1.9GB — that explains very slow dequeues. Those requests need long KV builds so they block batching for everyone.
sre-bot: alert created: INCIDENT-2026-03015-6265432100 (queue_saturation)
chris: Immediate mitigations: 1) throttle Northbound concurrency at the gateway (client-side token bucket) 2) enable tenant-specific model fallback to a smaller-model variant (gpt-medium -> gpt-small-kvless) 3) drain backlog via `batcher-drain` and, if needed, restart the batcher worker on bp-03.
elaine: I pushed a short-term rate-limit: `rlimit set tenant=northbound rate=15/s burst=30` — applied 09:06 UTC. Also configured fallback policy to `gpt-small-kvless` for that tenant 09:08 UTC.
mike: Initiating graceful drain: `curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/batcher/bp-03/drain?timeout=120s` — drain started 09:09 UTC.
olga: We should avoid hard restart until drain completes; killing mid-flight could cause extra 5xxs. If drain fails in 2m, we'll rotate traffic to hosted-prod-4.
support: Northbound notified: we've applied short-term rate limits and fallback; working on full mitigation.
(09:10) elaine: After rate limit + fallback, gateway queue_depth dropped from ~500 -> ~120 over 90s. p95 back to ~600ms, p99 ~2.4s. No customer-facing errors reported after 09:12.
chris: Good. Postmortem action items: - Add per-tenant longseq detection and auto-fallback policy. - Increase visibility: emit `tenant.kv_size` metric with per-p90/p99 to trigger early throttles. - Revisit node queue_depth cap vs memory eviction strategy.
jaya: Also add a canary for model-variant fallback so we don't change semantics unexpectedly.
mike: For follow-up, I'll collect batcher traces for bp-03 and upload to the incident runbook.
elaine: Quick repro steps for QA (do not run on prod):
1) Create 8 concurrent requests with 8k token prompts against a test tenant.
2) Observe `batcher.debug` queued growth and kv_size growth.
3) Validate fallback kicks in and queue drains.
```
# repro script (trimmed)
for i in {1..8}; do curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" https://hosted-api.test/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"<8k tokens>"}' & done
```
chris: Timeline note: root spike started 09:02, mitigations live by 09:09, stable by 09:12. I'll create an incident ticket and link this thread.
support: Northbound accepts the temporary fallback; requesting a patch to prevent unexpected cost/perf impact in future.
elaine: Closing here after runbook + follow-ups assigned. Thanks all.
(09:24) sre-bot: INCIDENT-2026-03015-6265432100 marked RESOLVED by chris
(09:30) jaya: I'll own the follow-up: add tenant.kv_size metric and the auto-fallback rule draft.
(09:32) olga: I'll write the knowledge base article for support teams on how to explain fallback vs throttling to customers.
(09:45) mike: Saved bp-03 traces to s3://redwood-incidents/6265432100/traces.tar.gz
